description: A comprehensive study of the fundamental principles of analog and digital communication, modulation techniques, noise analysis, and information theory.

sections.title: Amplitude Modulation (AM)
sections.description: An analog modulation technique where the amplitude of a high-frequency carrier wave is varied in accordance with the instantaneous amplitude of the modulating message signal.

sections.title: Angle Modulation (FM and PM)
sections.description: Analysis of Frequency Modulation (FM) and Phase Modulation (PM), where the phase angle of the carrier wave is varied proportionately with the message signal.

Pre-emphasis is used at the transmitter to artificially boost the power of higher-frequency message signals to improve the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR). De-emphasis is used at the receiver to attenuate these frequencies back to their original levels, thereby suppressing high-frequency noise.

sections.title: Sampling and Pulse Modulation
sections.description: The fundamental process of converting a continuous-time analog signal into a discrete-time, discrete-amplitude digital signal (Pulse Code Modulation).

key_concepts.explanation: States that a band-limited continuous-time signal can be perfectly recovered from its samples if the sampling frequency (fs) is at least twice the highest frequency component (fm) present in the signal.

A distortion phenomenon that occurs when the sampling rate is less than the Nyquist rate (fs < 2*fm). High-frequency components fold back and overlap onto low-frequency components, making original signal recovery impossible. Prevented by using a low-pass Anti-Aliasing Filter before sampling.

steps.title: Sampling
steps.detail: Discretizing the analog signal in the time domain at regular intervals (Ts).

steps.title: Quantization
steps.detail: Rounding off the sampled amplitudes to the nearest pre-determined discrete quantization level. This unavoidable approximation introduces Quantization Noise.

steps.title: Encoding
steps.detail: Converting the quantized discrete values into a sequence of binary bits (0s and 1s) for digital transmission.

sections.title: Digital Modulation Techniques
sections.description: Techniques used to map discrete digital data (binary sequences) onto an analog carrier wave for efficient transmission over bandpass channels.

results: ASK (Amplitude Shift Keying): The carrier is present for binary '1' and absent for binary '0' (ON-OFF Keying). It is highly susceptible to noise.
FSK (Frequency Shift Keying): Two distinct carrier frequencies are used to represent binary '1' and binary '0'. Constant envelope makes it more robust than ASK.
BPSK (Binary Phase Shift Keying): The phase of the carrier is shifted by 180 degrees to represent transitions between '1' and '0'. Highly robust and widely used.
QPSK (Quadrature Phase Shift Keying): Uses four distinct phase shifts (separated by 90 degrees) to transmit 2 bits per symbol, effectively doubling the bandwidth efficiency compared to BPSK.
